title: JRE 2277 - Woody Harrelson
guestBio: Woody Harrelson is an actor, playwright, and activist. Watch him in his new movie "Last Breath" only in theaters on February 28.
tldr: Woody Harrelson discusses his new film Last Breath and what drew him to the underwater survival thriller project
Conversation covers Woody's activism and his willingness to speak out on issues that most Hollywood figures treat as too risky
Discussion of consciousness, psychedelics, and how expanded states of awareness have shaped Woody's worldview and sense of purpose
Joe and Woody compare notes on health and diet and their shared belief that what you put in your body fundamentally matters
Harrelson reflects on how the entertainment industry has changed across decades and what has been gained and lost in the streaming era
Conversation explores Woody's plant-based lifestyle, his environmental commitments, and why he's dedicated to living according to his values
recap:
Woody Harrelson comes in to talk about his new film Last Breath, hitting theaters February 28, but the conversation with Joe goes much deeper than a standard press junket. Woody has never been someone who does the routine promotional interview. He shows up with his actual opinions about the world and isn't shy about sharing them, which is why he and Joe always produce something worth listening to.

They talk about Last Breath and what attracted Woody to the project, a survival thriller about divers trapped in extreme conditions. He walks through what the character demanded and why stories about people pushed to the absolute limit of their endurance resonate with audiences in ways that more comfortable narratives don't. The physical and emotional demands of the role, what it was like working through those extremes on set, all of it comes up naturally.

From there the conversation opens up into Woody's broader philosophy on life, which is where these conversations always get most interesting. Woody has been vocal about his views on everything from diet and health to corporate power and political systems, and he doesn't dial any of that back for Joe. They discuss his activism and why he feels compelled to speak publicly on issues that most people in Hollywood treat as career risks.

The conversation gets into consciousness and psychedelics, a subject Woody has explored personally and one that Joe always digs into with willing guests. Woody talks about how expanded states of awareness have shaped his view of what matters and how he moves through the world. It's a genuine philosophical discussion, not celebrity name-dropping.

Joe and Woody also spend time on health. Woody has maintained a plant-based lifestyle for decades, and Joe approaches health optimization from his own angle. They find common ground in the underlying principle that what you put in your body matters enormously even while coming at the specifics differently. It's one of those conversations that works precisely because they're not just agreeing with each other.

The episode also covers the entertainment industry and how it has transformed. Woody's career spans major shifts in how movies get made and distributed, and he has a genuine perspective on what's been gained and lost as Hollywood has evolved. He is honest about the trade-offs without being bitter about any of it.
